larosa023/hangar.name: Hangar v0.1.7
larosa023/hangar.body:
## Hangar 0.1.7

**Tray apps update now.** Some apps (Lumora, for one) only hide to the tray when asked to close, so their updates failed with "didn't close". Hangar now offers to force-close the app and finish the update. It only does that if you say yes.

## Also in this update (0.1.6): smoother and lighter

**Faster drawing**
- Text is laid out once and reused instead of on every frame. That was the most expensive part of drawing, so scrolling, hover effects and page changes do much less work per frame.
- Hangar no longer reads the disk or the registry while drawing. Previous Hangar versions, system colors and cleaned-up release notes are now read once.

**Lighter in the background**
- Background work runs on a few shared worker threads instead of one thread per job: 4 instead of about 50 at startup. Idle workers exit after a minute.
- "Running" detection checks every 2.5 seconds while Hangar is in front, and every 7 seconds when it isn't.
- Minimizing Hangar stops all polling and hands its memory back to Windows.
- Switching back to Hangar no longer re-scans every Start menu shortcut. Refresh (F5) still does a full scan.
- App icons are held only on the GPU instead of in both places.

**Refinements**
- **Crisper text:** solid themes now use ClearType. See-through themes (Mica, Glass) keep grayscale smoothing, because Windows requires it for transparency.
- Animations run at the same speed at any frame rate, and turn off when Windows' **Animation effects** setting is off.
- The **scrollbar** widens when you point at it, can be dragged, and clicking its track jumps a page.
- A soft shadow appears under the app card you're pointing at.
- **Ctrl+A** in search selects everything, so the next key replaces it.

larosa023/hangar.body:
## Hangar 0.1.5

**No more "GitHub limit reached".** Without a GitHub sign-in, GitHub allows only 60 release checks an hour, and Hangar was using 22 per refresh while sharing that budget with your apps' own updaters. Now:
- A job in the Hangar repo collects every app's releases into one file every 10 minutes.
- Hangar downloads that one file, which isn't counted against the limit, instead of calling GitHub once per app.
- If the file is ever missing or out of date, Hangar falls back to asking GitHub directly, as before.

Downloads are still verified against each release's SHA-256.

**Isle** has joined the library under Windows replacements.

larosa023/hangar.name: Hangar v0.1.4
larosa023/hangar.body:
## Hangar 0.1.4

**Themes.** A new **Themes** page in the sidebar has 14 themes with live previews. Click one and it changes right away.
- **Dark, Light,** and **Windows** (follows Windows light/dark mode)
- **Midnight:** pure black for OLED screens
- **Glass:** see-through over your wallpaper (Windows 11)
- **Frost, Twilight, Forest, Sunset, Ocean, Rose, Graphite**
- **Paper** and **Mist:** two softer light themes

**Accent color:** the theme's own, your Windows accent, 9 swatches, or any custom color.

**Theme files:** save the current look as a `.json` file to tweak or share it. Any theme files you drop in the themes folder show up in the gallery. See docs/THEMES.md for the format.

larosa023/hangar.name: Hangar v0.1.3
larosa023/hangar.body:
## Hangar 0.1.3

### Fixed
- **An app could keep showing "Update available" right after updating.** If an app's exe still carried an old version number in its file properties, Hangar believed the old number. Hangar now remembers exactly which release it installed and trusts that as long as the file hasn't changed. (Foyer 0.2.0 was the first app to hit this.)
- **Apps you downloaded but never "installed" now show as installed.** Hangar now also looks in your Downloads folder and on your Desktop, including renamed copies like `Breaker (1).exe`. It only accepts an exe whose file properties name the app or larosa023, so an unrelated file with a similar name is never picked up.

### Also
- Hangar's own version number is now stamped into Hangar.exe automatically on every build.

larosa023/hangar.name: Hangar v0.1.2
larosa023/hangar.body:
## Hangar 0.1.2

**Hangar now updates itself.**
- It checks GitHub for new versions of Hangar in the background: about 20 seconds after it opens, then on the same interval as app checks (every 3 hours by default).
- New versions download and are SHA-256 verified quietly. When one is ready, the sidebar shows **Restart to update**.
- Restarting takes about a second, and you land on the same page with the same search and scroll position. A short "What's new" note appears afterwards.
- **Automatic installs** wait until Hangar is minimized or you've been away from the PC for 2 minutes. Hangar never updates itself while it's installing apps.
- **Safe:** if a new version doesn't start, Hangar puts the old one back by itself and skips that version.
- **Roll back** to either of the last 2 versions from Settings → Hangar updates.
- **Stable or Beta** channel for Hangar itself, and auto-install can be turned off.

You need to download this version by hand once. From here on, Hangar keeps itself up to date.

larosa023/hangar.name: Hangar v0.1.1
larosa023/hangar.body:
## Hangar 0.1.1

**Finds your apps wherever they are.** Before, Hangar only looked in each app's standard install folder, so apps you run from somewhere else showed "Install". Now it also checks:
- apps that are running right now
- startup entries (the Windows "Run" list) and Start menu, desktop and taskbar shortcuts
- common folders: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<App>`, `%APPDATA%\<App>`, `Program Files`
- Apps & features entries whose icon isn't the exe (fixes Gridline)

Hangar checks each exe's version info so it doesn't mistake another program with the same file name for one of yours, and it remembers where each app was found. If an app still isn't found, open its page and click **Already installed? Locate it**.

larosa023/hangar.name: Hangar v0.1.0
larosa023/hangar.body:
## Hangar 0.1.0 (Phase 1)

The first build of Hangar, home base for the larosa023 apps.

- **Library** of all 21 apps in the suite, in a grid or a list, with categories, search (Ctrl+K) and keyboard navigation. It opens straight away from a cache, then refreshes in the background.
- **Shows what's installed and running**, including apps you installed before Hangar existed.
- **Release checks** against each app's GitHub Releases, on the Stable or Beta channel, with very little use of GitHub's rate limit.
- **One-click Install, Open, Update, Repair and Uninstall.** It handles single-exe apps, NSIS setups (Electron and Tauri apps) and Velopack setups.
- **Verified downloads:** SHA-256 against GitHub's digest and the app's own checksum file.
- **Updating an open app:** Hangar closes it the normal way, updates it, and reopens it. If the new version doesn't start, the previous one comes back.
- **Update all**, a page per app with release history, and Settings (theme, default channel, check interval, local manifest).

larosa023/foyer.name: Foyer v0.3.1
larosa023/foyer.body:
## Foyer 0.3.1 — refinement and performance

Tuned against a week of real usage logs.

### Faster
- **Complete from the first press after boot.** The app list is saved and loads instantly, instead of showing "Loading apps" for about two seconds while Windows enumerates apps.
- **File search works immediately at startup.** The file index is saved to disk and reused, instead of being rebuilt from scratch first.
- **Smoother across monitors.** Moving the menu to a monitor with different scaling no longer rebuilds every icon (that was behind the slowest opens, up to about 60 ms).
- **Typing is lighter.** File search waits for a brief pause in typing instead of searching the disk on every keystroke.

### Much less background work
- Foyer now **watches for changes** instead of re-checking on every open: the app list refreshes only when a Start menu shortcut or a Store app changes, Recent only when you open a file, and the file index only when your folders actually change. (Last week Foyer re-scanned all apps 161 times and rebuilt the file index 47 times. Now it's only when something changed.)
- The taskbar Start button is located again only when a taskbar moves or its alignment changes, instead of on many clicks and setting changes.

### Fixed
- **File search could be unavailable for 30–50 minutes.** Foyer pauses background work while you game, but an ordinary maximized window (with an auto-hiding taskbar) looked like a fullscreen game. Only real borderless fullscreen apps count now. This also makes automatic updates wait less.
- **Typing sometimes went to the app behind Foyer** when Windows refused to give it focus. Foyer now retries until it gets focus.

larosa023/foyer.name: Foyer v0.3.0
larosa023/foyer.body:
## Foyer 0.3.0

### Search that finds everything
- **Files and folders** from your Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music, Videos and OneDrive. If [Everything](https://www.voidtools.com) is running, Foyer uses it and searches every drive instantly; otherwise it keeps its own small index that refreshes at low priority and pauses while you game.
- **Settings and Control Panel**: type "bluetooth", "display", "device manager", "environment variables" and jump straight there.
- **Calculator**: `12*7.5`, `20% of 50`, `sqrt(144)`, `(3+4)*2`. Enter copies the answer.
- **Unit conversions**, including construction units: `5 cy to cf`, `1250 sf to sy`, `12 ft to m`, `72 f in c`, `100 psi to kpa`.
- **Prefixes**: `f:` files only, `s:` settings only, `a:` apps only, `>` run a command (Ctrl+Shift+Enter runs it as administrator).
- Results are grouped (Best match, Apps, Settings, Files & folders) and **things you open often move up** over time.

### Recent
- Recently opened files and folders only, never "recently added" apps. Right-click to pin one or remove it; turn Recent off in Settings.

### Pinning
- **Drag** tiles to reorder them, and drag apps, files and search results onto Pinned to pin them.
- **Folders**: drop one tile onto another to group them. Rename or ungroup any time.
- **Rename** any tile (F2) and give it a **custom icon** (.ico, .png, .exe, .dll).
- **Pin files, folders and websites**, not just apps (right-click the Pinned area).
- **My Apps**: an automatic folder with every larosa023 app on this PC.

### Everything else
- **Bottom bar shortcuts**: choose up to 6 (Downloads, Documents, Task Manager, Device Manager, Terminal, Recycle Bin and more) in Settings, Layout.
- **Instant icons after boot**: icons are cached on disk.
- **Theme files**: export your look as a small JSON file, import and share themes.
- **Font picker** and **text size**.
- **Accessibility**: Narrator reads the selected item and the search box; high contrast, Windows text size and "animation effects off" are respected.
- **Work over admin windows** (optional): Foyer can start as administrator at sign-in so it opens even when an admin app is focused. Apps you launch still run as you, not as administrator.
- **Installer**: Foyer can install itself to your Programs folder, the Start menu and Apps & features, and uninstall cleanly. Portable mode still works.

larosa023/foyer.name: Foyer v0.2.2
larosa023/foyer.body:
## Foyer 0.2.2

### Fixed
- **Apps without a Start menu shortcut now show up.** Windows only lists apps that have a Start menu shortcut, so portable apps run from Downloads, Documents or a tools folder were missing from both Foyer and the Windows Start menu. Foyer now also lists every larosa023 app that Hangar knows about, wherever it lives, with its proper name and icon. Search, pinning, Run as administrator and Open file location all work for them.

larosa023/foyer.name: Foyer v0.2.1
larosa023/foyer.body:
## Foyer 0.2.1

### Fixed
- **Hangar kept offering the 0.2.0 update after installing it.** The 0.2.0 exe still said "0.1.0" in its file properties, which Windows and Hangar read. The version is now stamped into the exe automatically on every build, so this can't happen again.

### How to update
Click **Update** on Foyer in Hangar, or let Foyer's built-in updater install it.

larosa023/foyer.name: Foyer v0.2.0
larosa023/foyer.body:
## Foyer 0.2.0

### New
- **Settings window** — General, Appearance, Layout, Apps, Updates and About pages. Changes apply instantly, with a live preview of the menu.
- **Built-in updater** — checks GitHub Releases, verifies every download with SHA-256, installs with one click (or automatically), and rolls back by itself if a new version fails to start. Stable and Beta channels. Never interrupts games or fullscreen video.
- **Themes** — Follow Windows, Dark, Light, Midnight (pure black), Glass, Ember and Ocean, plus an accent color picker.
- **Acrylic and Mica** backgrounds with adjustable tint, and adjustable corner radius.
- **Layouts** — Modern (pinned grid + All apps), Classic (single column) and Full screen (launcher overlay). Choose position, density and icon size.
- **Motion** — slide-in open, staggered tiles, smooth hover fades, press feedback, smooth scrolling and tooltips. Turn it down to Fast or None any time.
- **Greeting** with your name and today's date, and a soft accent glow.
- **Backup and restore** of all settings to one file.

### How to update from 0.1.0
0.1.0 has no updater yet: quit Foyer from the tray, then run this Foyer.exe. From 0.2.0 on, updates install themselves.

larosa023/strata.name: Strata v0.3.5
larosa023/strata.body:
## Strata 0.3.5

- **Drag tabs out into their own window**, like a web browser. Pull a tab down or off the tab bar, and a small preview follows the cursor. Let go and the tab opens in a new Strata window right there, keeping both of its panes, its tab color and its lock.

larosa023/strata.name: Strata v0.3.4
larosa023/strata.body:

  - A normal double-click still opens it.
  - Dragging, pressing a key, or clicking somewhere else cancels the rename.

larosa023/strata.name: Strata v0.3.3
larosa023/strata.body:
## Strata 0.3.3

- **Fixed: updates wouldn't install while Strata was maximized.** The updater waits for full-screen games and videos to close before installing. A maximized Strata window also fills the screen, so Strata mistook itself for a game and kept postponing. Now:
  - Strata's own windows and normal maximized windows don't count as full-screen.
  - Clicking **Update** installs straight away. The only thing it still waits for is a file transfer in progress, and it tells you when that's the case.

Also in 0.3.2: menus drawn in Strata's theme (rounded, acrylic, icons, accent checks), and a tidier ⋯ menu with View and Appearance submenus.

larosa023/strata.body:

  - Rounded cards with an acrylic blur on Windows 11.

larosa023/strata.name: Strata v0.3.1
larosa023/strata.body:

larosa023/strata.name: Strata v0.3.0
larosa023/strata.body:
## Strata 0.3.0

**Made for bid folders**
- **Version stacking:** `Plans_rev1.pdf`, `Plans_rev2.pdf` and `Plans rev 3.pdf` collapse into one row that shows the newest, with a **"3 versions"** pill. Click the pill, or press **→**, to see the older versions underneath. It understands rev/R/v numbers, revision letters (Rev B), dates (`_2026-03-01`), `(2)` and `- Copy`. Sheet numbers like `A-101` are left alone. You can turn it off in Settings → Layout.
- **What changed (Ctrl+Shift+H):** every file in this folder and its subfolders that changed **since your last visit**, today, in the last 7 or 30 days, or since a date. Newest files come first. Esc goes back.
- **Space view (Ctrl+Shift+S, or the 4th view button):** a treemap of what's using space, colored by kind (drawings, PDFs and Office files, video, images, archives). Double-click a folder to look inside. On This PC it shows your drives. Every folder and drive also has "Show what's using space" on its right-click menu.

**Everyday speed**
- **Quick look carousel:** press **Space** for a big preview, then use ← → to flip through files. Enter opens the file; Space or Esc closes the preview.
- **Jump to folder (Ctrl+G):** a fuzzy search over the folders you use, ranked by how often and how recently you opened them. Type "smi bid" to reach `D:\Bids\2026\Smith Library`. Ctrl+Enter opens it in a new tab, Shift+Enter in the other pane. Grid view moved to **Ctrl+Shift+G**.
- **Focus filter (Ctrl+Shift+F):** show only PDFs, drawings, Office files, images, files changed this week, files with a given tag, or the same type as the selection. The filter stays on while you browse; Esc or ✕ turns it off.
- **Tabs that stick:** right-click a tab → **Lock tab to this folder**. Folders you open from a locked tab open in a new tab. Right-click a tab → **Tab color** to color it.

**Polish**
- **Smooth animations:** the active tab and the active pane's accent bar slide, the sidebar and preview slide in and out, and folders fade in. Choose None / Fast / Smooth in Settings → Layout; Strata also follows Windows' "Animation effects" setting.
- **Themed dialogs:** replace/skip conflicts, delete confirmations, update notes, uninstall and name prompts now use your theme instead of plain Windows boxes. The batch rename window is themed too.
- **Sounds and notifications:** when a copy or move that took longer than 10 seconds finishes, Strata plays a soft chime and shows a card with **Open folder**. If Strata isn't in front, you get a Windows notification instead. You can turn both off in Settings → File operations.

larosa023/strata.name: Strata v0.2.2
larosa023/strata.body:
## Strata 0.2.2

- **Rearrange the sidebar:** drag pinned folders, drives, tags and saved searches to reorder them, or drag a section header (Pinned, Drives, Tags, Saved searches, Recent) to move the whole section. A line shows where it will land. Right-click also has **Move up / Move down**, and right-clicking a header offers **Reset sidebar order**.
- The order, and which sections are collapsed, are remembered.

larosa023/strata.body:

Windows was drawing its own caption buttons into the see-through title bar; Strata now tells Windows not to draw them at all (the same fix Firefox uses). larosa023/strata.name: Strata v0.2.0
larosa023/strata.body:
## Strata 0.2.0 — the big one

Everything from the remaining roadmap phases lands in this release.

**Dual pane & keyboard**
- Dual-pane layout (default) with **Tab** to switch panes, **F5** copy / **F6** move to the other pane, and a view switch for dual, single, and grid.
- Grid view with thumbnails. Strata remembers sort order, view, and columns for each folder.
- Columns adapt to narrow panes.

**Transfers**
- Strata's own transfer queue: pause, resume, cancel, and skip, with speed and ETA. **Ctrl+J** opens the transfers panel.
- Optional SHA-256 **verify after copy**. Strata warns when the destination is low on space and lets you set a default for name conflicts.
- **Ctrl+Z undo** for rename, move, copy, new folder, and delete (deleted items come back from the Recycle Bin).
- **Batch rename:** press F2 with several items selected. You can find and replace (with optional regex), add a prefix or suffix, number items, and change case, with a live preview. Ctrl+Z undoes the whole batch.
- Drag and drop between panes, tabs, the sidebar, and other apps.

**Folder sizes & tags**
- Folder sizes are calculated in the background, with size bars. This pauses while you're gaming or the CPU is busy.
- Color tags on files and folders: Urgent, Active, Done, and Repo, plus your own. Click a tag in the sidebar to see everything with that tag.

**Search**
- Search uses **Everything** if it's running; otherwise it uses Strata's own whole-PC index, which rebuilds in the background.
- Filters: `type:pdf`, `ext:dwg`, `size:>50mb`, `modified:7d`, `modified:2026-03`, `tag:urgent`, `folder:`, and `file:`.
- **Saved searches** become smart folders in the sidebar.

**Preview panel** (Ctrl+P, or Space for a quick look)
- Images, text and code, PDF, Office files, and video through the Windows preview handlers.
- File details, plus "what's taking space" for folders.
- **Git status** (branch, changes, ahead/behind), with buttons for Open and Open in other pane.

**Archives:** browse into .zip files like folders, and extract with drag-out or **Extract here**.

**Right-click menu:** a cleaner menu that hides clutter you choose (hold **Shift** to see everything), plus Open in other pane, Calculate size, Copy path, Open terminal, and Add tag.

**Settings window** (Ctrl+,): General, Layout, Themes, Search, Tags, File operations, Updates, and About.
- Theme presets and a custom theme with live preview, plus accent color, Mica or Acrylic backdrop, font, size, corner radius, and density.
- Theme files can be imported and exported, and are compatible with Foyer.

**System**
- **Built-in updater:** Stable and Beta channels, SHA-256 check, and automatic rollback if a new version fails to start. It never installs during a transfer or while you're gaming. Future versions install themselves.
- Install to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` (Start menu entry, uninstall from Apps) or run in portable mode.
- Start with Windows, with a tray icon and close to tray.
- Optional **default file manager** (folders and Win+E open in Strata) with a safe fallback. If Strata crashes or hangs, folders open in File Explorer, and `Strata.exe --restore-explorer` undoes it.
- Back up and restore settings, pins, tags, and folder views as one file.
- Respects Windows high-contrast mode and text scaling.

larosa023/loupe.name: Loupe v0.1.0
larosa023/loupe.body:
## Loupe 0.1.0

The first release of Loupe, a fast, modern replacement for the Windows 11 Photos app.

### Viewing
- **Opens in a blink.** The first image starts decoding before the window exists, and JPEGs decode straight to screen size.
- **Flip without blank frames.** Arrow keys, Page Up/Down or the mouse wheel move through the folder, with the next and previous images already decoded. Sort by name, date taken, date modified or size.
- **Zoom** to fit or 100%, scroll-to-zoom at the cursor, drag to pan, double-click to toggle. Full resolution loads in the background when you zoom past the screen-sized image.
- **Animated GIF, WebP and APNG**, with pause and frame stepping.
- **Filmstrip** (F), **grid** of the whole folder (G), **info panel** (I) with camera, lens, exposure and GPS, and **compare** (C) with synced zoom and pan.
- **Slideshow** (Space) and full screen (F11).
- JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, HEIC, BMP, TIFF, ICO, SVG, and RAW previews for CR2, CR3, NEF, ARW and DNG. Color profiles and EXIF orientation are applied.

### Editing
- Crop with preset ratios, rotate, flip, straighten, and exposure, contrast, saturation and warmth.
- Save asks before replacing the original, and Ctrl+Z can put the original back. Save a copy, or Revert.

### Files
- Copy image or path, show in Explorer, open in Strata, set as wallpaper, print, Open with.
- Delete to the Recycle Bin with undo, rename (F2), drag and drop.

### The suite

## Breaker 1.2.0

### New: Screen time
A new **Screen time** section in the sidebar shows where your time goes, app by app and game by game.

- **Counts only real use:** it notes which app is in front every 5 seconds. Time doesn't count when there's no input for 2 minutes (unless a game or video is playing), or while the PC is locked or asleep.
- **Keeps counting when Breaker is closed:** a tiny background tracker (`Breaker.exe --tracker`) starts with Windows. It has no window, runs at low priority, wakes once every 5 seconds and saves every few minutes.
- **Knows your games:** anything from Steam, Epic, GOG, the Xbox app or RetroArch, or running full screen, is tagged as a game and shown under its real name (from Steam's and Epic's own records and GOG's registry entries), not the exe name.
- **Categories:** Games, Work, Browsing, Media, Chat and Other are picked automatically; change any app's category from its page.
- **Daily limits:** for an app or a whole category, with a gentle notification at 80% and 100%. Nothing is ever closed or blocked.
- **Weekly summary** notification (on or off), and **export to CSV**.
- **Privacy:** a never-track list, and "Clear history" for today, the last 7 days, a date range or everything. Everything stays in plain files in Breaker's data folder, and nothing leaves the PC.

larosa023/caption.name: Caption v0.3.3
larosa023/caption.body:
## Caption 0.3.3

**Ripple subtitles stay in step.**

- **Switching audio tracks no longer breaks the subtitles.** Caption now starts over on the new track behind the same subtitle address, so Ripple keeps one "AI subtitles" track that simply fills in again (needs Ripple 1.2.3).
- **No more starting over from the beginning by mistake.** A stray "position 0" from the player while a stream reloads used to make Caption throw away its place and re-do the movie from 0:00. A jump now has to be confirmed by a second report.
- **Accurate "ready to" time.** The status line shows how far subtitles are ready from where you're actually watching.

larosa023/caption.name: Caption v0.3.2
larosa023/caption.body:
## Caption 0.3.2

**Ripple subtitles: fewer missed lines, tighter timing, cleaner layout.**

Measured against the official subtitles of Blender's open movie *Tears of Steel* (dialogue over music and effects), with a new automated test that runs on every change:

- **Fewer missed lines.** Speech is now detected on both the dialogue (center) channel and the full mix, with more sensitive thresholds, so lines said over loud music and effects get through. Lines caught went from about 72% to 77–79%.
- **Timing that follows the voice.** Each line now starts when the voice starts (with a tiny lead so your eye catches it) and ends when it stops, instead of hanging on into the pause. Subtitle ends within half a second of the official ones went from 42% to about 72%.
- **Layout like a subtitler's.** One line when it fits; otherwise two lines broken after punctuation or before "and", "but", "that"…, never after "the", "a", "my" and the like. Two short sentences said back to back share a subtitle, one per line, and short gaps between lines are closed so the screen doesn't blink. Subtitles that went by faster than you can read dropped from 15% to 4%.
- **No more "Thanks for watching."** Whisper's habit of inventing YouTube outros and subtitle credits over music is filtered out.

larosa023/caption.name: Caption v0.3.1
larosa023/caption.body:
## Caption 0.3.1

**Ripple subtitles keep up from the first minute.**

- **No more gap after the first line.** Caption used to wait for 75 seconds of audio before making the next batch of subtitles, which on big remux files meant playback overtook it. It now works in short pieces while playback is close behind and switches to longer ones once it's comfortably ahead.
- **Clearer log.** Each step of a Ripple subtitle job (how long the audio took to download and transcribe, and how far ahead of playback it is) is written to the log, along with when a job stops.

larosa023/caption.name: Caption v0.3.0
larosa023/caption.body:
## Caption 0.3.0

**Real subtitles for Ripple, timed to the word.**

- **Subtitles made ahead of playback.** When a movie or episode starts in Ripple, Ripple hands Caption the stream. Caption reads the audio ahead of the playhead and runs Whisper on each stretch of speech with up to 25 seconds of context, with word timing taken from Whisper's own attention. The result is laid out like professional subtitles: one sentence per subtitle, two balanced lines of up to 42 characters, no overlaps. It shows up in Ripple's subtitle menu as "AI subtitles" and keeps filling in a few minutes ahead of where you are. Seeking works.
- **Music and silence are never transcribed.** Voice detection picks out the speech first, so no invented lines over the score or the credits. Dialogue focus (center channel / center extraction) is used here too.
- **Uses your most accurate model.** Pick it in Speech model → Subtitles for Ripple. Large v3 is the best choice here, since subtitles don't need to be live.
- **Live captions step aside** while Ripple shows Caption's subtitles, so you never get two sets.
- The first time, Caption downloads FFmpeg (about 80 MB) to read stream audio.
- Everything stays on your PC: the subtitle service only answers apps on this computer.

larosa023/caption.name: Caption v0.1.1
larosa023/caption.body:
## Caption 0.1.1

Much more accurate captions that keep up with the speaker.

- **Whole sentences, not fragments.** Whisper now always hears the sentence so far, with the previous lines as context, instead of short clips cut at every little pause. Far fewer wrong or made-up words, and better names, casing and punctuation.
- **Words appear as they're spoken.** The line is re-read every 0.3 s. Each word turns solid as soon as two reads agree on it; only the newest few words stay dimmed while they might still change. Lines end at real sentence ends.
- **More accurate on the GPU.** Beam search is on when Caption runs on your GPU.
- **"English (Whisper)" only translates speech that isn't English.** English stays as it was spoken; translating it again made captions worse.
- Your listening settings move to the new defaults (update every 0.3 s, a 0.9 s pause ends a line) unless you had changed them.

larosa023/caption.name: Caption v0.1.0

The first release: live captions and translation for anything playing on your PC, running 100% locally on your GPU.

larosa023/haul.body:
- Jackett is built in too, the same way as Prowlarr: Haul finds it, reads its key, starts it hidden when you search and searches every site you've added in it (its "all" feed). Settings → Torrent search shows how many sites it has, with an **Add sites…** button.
- If Jackett has no FlareSolverr address set (and no admin password), Haul fills in FlareSolverr's address for it.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.4.7
larosa023/haul.body: - Settings → Torrent search: **Add sites…** opens Prowlarr's page again (the click did nothing because Haul only opened https links). It starts Prowlarr first if it isn't running.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.4.6
larosa023/haul.body:
- Prowlarr is built in. Haul finds Prowlarr on your PC, reads its address and API key by itself, starts it hidden when you search (no window or browser tab to keep open) and searches every site you've added to it in one go. No Torznab links or keys to copy any more; links added by hand to the same Prowlarr are skipped so nothing is searched twice.
- Sites Prowlarr has paused after errors are re-tested before each search, so they come back on their own.
- Haul also finds FlareSolverr one folder deeper in Downloads, Desktop and Documents.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.4.5
larosa023/haul.body:
- Torrent search: while a search runs, the previous results fade out and Haul says what it's searching for (and why when it's slow), so old results can't be mistaken for new ones. The result count says which search it's for.
- When Prowlarr has benched an indexer after failures (for example while FlareSolverr was still starting), Haul asks Prowlarr to re-test its indexers and searches again by itself. If it's still benched, the message says so in plain words.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.4.4
larosa023/haul.body:
- The details panel hides when nothing is selected and nothing is downloading or uploading, so the list gets the whole window. It comes back when something starts or when you select a download.
- Blocks style: a near-zero speed no longer draws a stray bar in the corner of the graph.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.4.3
larosa023/haul.body:
- The details panel follows your download tracking style too: the speed graph is a soft glow, a plain line, moving stripes, an aurora, retro bars, a hairline or neon, and the live card changes to match. The style tiles in Settings → Appearance preview the graph as well.
- With nothing selected, the details panel shows a live overview instead of an empty space: total speed with a graph, peak, what's downloading, queued and seeding, what finished today, and the active downloads (click one to open it).

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.4.2
larosa023/haul.body:
- Torrent search: PC and console games are labelled **Games** (they showed as Software).
- FlareSolverr starts by itself: before a search Haul checks it's running and, if not, starts it hidden (no window). Haul finds it in your Startup folder or the usual unzip places, or you can point to it in Settings → Torrent search.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.4.1
larosa023/haul.body: - Torrent search: when a site says it's getting too many searches (429), Haul waits and tries again by itself, and otherwise explains it in plain words.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.4.0
larosa023/haul.body:
- **Torrent search** (sidebar → Search, or `Ctrl+K`). Searches Internet Archive (built in) and any Torznab indexers you add from Prowlarr or Jackett, all at once. Results are merged, de-duplicated and sorted by seeders, with size, age and a seed-health dot; filter by category or text, and download straight away (or through your debrid service). Add sources in Settings → Torrent search.
- **More debrid services:** AllDebrid, Premiumize and TorBox, alongside Real-Debrid. Each keeps its own key; pick the one Haul uses in Settings → Debrid. File hoster links and torrents work with all four (choosing files before the download starts is Real-Debrid only).
- **Duplicate warning:** the New download and video windows tell you when you already downloaded a link (with Open / Show it), batches can skip links already in your list, and a link from the browser or clipboard that you already have opens the New download window so you see the warning.
- **Download tracking styles:** Glow, Classic, Striped, Aurora, Blocks, Minimal or Neon, with live previews in Settings → Appearance. They apply to the list, the connection map and the mini window.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.3.2
larosa023/haul.body: - Safety score: the "digitally signed by…" check for programs now works on every PC (it could fail when PowerShell 7 is installed). Programs signed by a verified publisher score higher.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.3.1
larosa023/haul.body:
- **Safety score.** Every download gets a grade from A (looks safe) to F (likely dangerous), with the reasons listed under it.
  - When you paste a link: is it encrypted, is the site a bare IP, a look-alike name, a short link or a scam-prone domain, is it a program, and is the name disguised (like `invoice.pdf.exe` or hidden reversed text)?
  - When it finishes: does the content match its name (a program posing as a video gets an F), is a program digitally signed and by whom, what's inside archives (programs, disguised names, passwords), and a Windows Defender scan. Dangerous files aren't auto-extracted, and you get a warning.
  - Optional VirusTotal check with your own free key (only the file's SHA-256 is sent).
  - Downloads are now marked as from the internet, like browsers do, so SmartScreen and Office Protected View work on them.
  - Settings → Safety turns each part on or off.
- **Live download view.** A live speed graph with peak and average, and a map of every connection filling its part of the file. Running progress bars glow and shimmer, there's a speed graph behind the totals in the sidebar and in the mini window.
- **Speeds in Mbps** (Settings → Appearance), the unit internet plans use. 111 MB/s is about 930 Mbps.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.3.0
larosa023/haul.body:
- **Video and music downloads** from YouTube and the 1,800+ other sites yt-dlp supports. Paste a link (or use the browser button) and pick the quality, up to 8K and HDR as MP4, or audio only as MP3, M4A or Opus. Options for subtitles, chapters, embedded thumbnails and SponsorBlock (skip or mark sponsor segments). Playlists and channels list their videos so you can pick which to queue. Videos go to your Video folder and audio to Music, by the sorting rules.
  - Haul downloads yt-dlp and ffmpeg the first time you need them (they aren't bundled), checks their SHA-256, and keeps yt-dlp up to date by itself, right away when a site stops working. Settings → Video & music shows their versions, with Update now and Remove.
- **HLS (.m3u8) and DASH (.mpd) streams**: the pieces download in parallel and are joined into one file.
- **FTP and FTPS** links (ftp://, ftps://, ftpes://), with multiple connections and resume.
- **Smarter resume**: before resuming, Haul checks the file hasn't changed on the server (ETag / Last-Modified). If it has, the download starts over cleanly instead of making a corrupted file.
- **Connections per download** can go up to 32, and the new default is **Auto**: 1 connection for small files, up to 24 for huge ones.
- **Batch downloads**: paste a list of links, or a pattern like `file[001-100].zip`, `part[a-f].rar` or `img[0-40:2].jpg`.
- **Site grabber**: give it a page and it lists every file the page links to, with sizes, filterable by type, size and name. Pick what to queue.
- **Hugging Face**: paste a model or dataset link (or `org/name`), pick the files (or "only .safetensors" / one GGUF), and they download over multiple connections, each checked against its SHA-256 (or git hash) when done. An optional token for gated and private models.
- **Firefox**: the browser extension now works in Firefox too, with the same features.
- **"Download video with Haul"** in the extension: a small button on video pages, a page right-click item, and a button in the popup.
- **Mini window**: a small always-on-top window with active downloads, total speed and Pause all. Toggle it from the tray or with `Ctrl+Alt+H` (change it in Settings → General).

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.2.0
larosa023/haul.body:
- Real-Debrid support. Connect your account in Settings → Debrid with your API key (stored encrypted for your Windows account).
  - Links from file hosters Real-Debrid supports download at premium speed, with Haul's multiple connections. Expired links are renewed automatically.
  - Torrents can be downloaded by Real-Debrid instead of your PC: pick the files, watch Real-Debrid's progress in the list, then Haul fetches the files at full speed, keeping the torrent's folders. Choose Off, Ask each time (a switch in the New download window) or Always.
- Magnet links and .torrent files you open from your browser or Explorer show the New download window when Real-Debrid is set to Ask each time.

larosa023/haul.name: Haul v0.1.0
larosa023/haul.body:
First release of Haul: direct downloads and torrents in one light app.

- Direct downloads split into parallel connections, resume after pauses and restarts, retry on failure, and can verify a SHA-256.
- Torrents (magnet links and .torrent files) with file picking, file priorities, sequential download, seeding ratio/time limits, DHT, PEX, encryption, UPnP and NAT-PMP, IP blocklists and binding to a network adapter (with a kill switch).
- One list for everything, with filters and search.
- Finished files sorted into folders by your rules; optional auto-extract of zip, 7z and rar.
- Global and per-download speed limits, a speed schedule and a queue.
- Browser extension for Chrome, Edge, Drift and other Chromium browsers.
- Notifications with Open and Show in folder.
- 14 suite themes, accent colors and custom theme files.
- Built-in updates with Stable and Beta channels, checksum checks and automatic rollback.

larosa023/rigcard.name: Rigcard v1.0.0
larosa023/rigcard.body:
## Rigcard 1.0.0

The first release: your PC build as one clean, shareable card.

- **Detects your hardware by itself**: CPU, GPU and VRAM, motherboard and BIOS, memory (size, speed, modules), drives, monitors, keyboard and mouse, Windows version. Rescan any time to see what changed.
- **Parts Windows can't see**: search-as-you-type picker for coolers, power supplies, cases, fans and peripherals, or type anything.
- **Live stats**: CPU and GPU temperature, clocks, load, power draw and uptime, read only while the window is open.
- **Benchmarks**: quick CPU single and multi-core, GPU compute, memory bandwidth and latency, storage read, write and 4K tests, with history. Import 3DMark, CrystalDiskMark, Geekbench and Cinebench scores.
- **Card design**: 10 styles, full color, font, layout and corner control, photo cropping, blurred photo backgrounds. Save and share styles as JSON.
- **Export** PNGs for Discord and Reddit, square posts, Instagram portrait, phone wallpapers and 4K. Copy the image straight to the clipboard.
- **Share links**: an instant quick link, or a hosted page (a secret gist on your GitHub) that updates when your build does, with optional live stats.
- **Privacy**: serial numbers, IP address, user name and location stay off the card unless you turn them on.
- Themes shared with the rest of the suite, live theme changes from Hangar, a built-in updater with Stable and Beta channels, hash-verified downloads and automatic rollback.

larosa023/outpost.name: Outpost v1.0.3
larosa023/outpost.body:
## Outpost 1.0.3

- Smooth scrolling and animations at your monitor's full refresh rate (60, 144, 165 Hz…). Outpost now draws in step with the screen instead of on a timer that topped out around 64 frames a second and stuttered against the display. Movement uses real elapsed time, so it feels the same on any monitor.
- Snappier scroll easing.
- The tray tooltip is only updated when it changes.
- If a frame ever takes too long to draw, Outpost notes it in outpost.log (Settings → About → Log file) to help track it down.

larosa023/outpost.name: Outpost v1.0.2
larosa023/outpost.body:
## Outpost 1.0.2

- Much smoother scrolling and hovering everywhere, especially in Settings: text layouts are now built once and reused, and text that's scrolled out of view isn't drawn at all.
- Fixed: in Outpost settings, the "a backup fails" switch was drawn on top of "a player joins". The three notification switches now each have their own row.
- Fixed: the UPnP switch in a server's Network settings could sit in the wrong place when its description wrapped.

larosa023/outpost.name: Outpost v1.0.1
larosa023/outpost.body:
## Outpost 1.0.1

- Settings pages are much smoother: text measurements are cached, and slow checks (old versions, Windows colors, Hangar) run every few seconds instead of every frame. Scrolling past switches no longer slows the app down over time.
- Outpost redraws only when something under the mouse changes.
- On wide or full-screen windows, Outpost settings, the new server wizard and each server's Settings tab are centered in a readable column.
- Fixed: the "you're playing a game" notice could appear when Outpost itself filled the screen.
- Fixed: Paper/Fabric config folders (like bStats or spark) were listed as plugins.
- The Restore button in the backup card no longer spills out of the card on narrow windows.

larosa023/outpost.name: Outpost v1.0.0
larosa023/outpost.body:
## Outpost 1.0.0

The first release: one-click game servers for Windows.

- **12 games**: Minecraft Java (Vanilla, Paper, Fabric, Forge, NeoForge), Minecraft Bedrock, Valheim, Palworld, Terraria, Satisfactory, Project Zomboid, Enshrouded, ARK: Survival Ascended, Rust, Counter-Strike 2 and 7 Days to Die. SteamCMD and Java are handled for you.
- **New server wizard**, import an existing server or world, any number of servers per game.
- **Live console** with colors, command history and autocomplete; players, CPU, RAM and TPS/FPS.
- **Players**: kick, ban, op, whitelist with buttons; join/leave history.
- **Mods**: Modrinth (and CurseForge with your key) for Minecraft, with compatibility checks and one-click updates; mod folders for other games; enable/disable without deleting.
- **Backups** on a schedule and on demand, keep the last N, any folder (an external drive or OneDrive), one-click restore with a safety backup first.
- **Networking**: UPnP port forwarding, Windows Firewall rules, NAT and reachability checks, router steps when UPnP isn't there, hide-my-IP, optional DuckDNS address.
- **Runs in the background**: servers keep running when Outpost closes or updates; auto-restart on crash, scheduled restarts, sleep when empty and wake on join.
- Themes from the suite (Dark, Light, Midnight, Glass and more), accent colors, density, corners, font size; live themes from Hangar.
- Built-in updater with Stable and Beta channels, verified downloads and automatic rollback.

larosa023/reticle.name: Reticle v0.1.3
larosa023/reticle.body:
## Reticle 0.1.3

**You pick which apps get the overlay.**

- Everything Reticle thinks is a game is listed on the **Games** page, each with its own **Overlay** and **Crosshair** switches.
- Newly found games start with the overlay **off**. The first time Reticle finds one, it shows a short note in the corner, for example "Minecraft found · Alt+Shift+O shows the overlay here". Press the shortcut and that game keeps the overlay from then on. To go back to automatic, turn on **Overlay → Turn the overlay on for newly found games**.
- **Games → Add a running app** lists your open app windows so you can pick one, even if Reticle didn't think it was a game. **Add .exe…** is still there too.
- The tray menu has **Overlay in *Game*** and ***App* isn't a game** for whatever is in front.
- Clicking **Restart to update** now installs right away, even if Reticle thinks a game is open. Automatic updates still wait until no game is running.
- Update checks now ask GitHub directly when Hangar's release list is out of date, so new versions show up right away.

larosa023/reticle.name: Reticle v0.1.2
larosa023/reticle.body:
## Reticle 0.1.2

- **Fixed:** whole numbers on the overlay (FPS, 1% and 0.1% lows, CPU and GPU %, temperatures, GB totals) always showed **0**. Frame capture was working; the numbers were printed wrong. Every release is now checked with a screenshot of the overlay over a running test game.
- **Fixed:** ordinary apps were being treated as games. 0.1.1 counted any big window that kept drawing for a few seconds, so apps like video players and launchers got the overlay. Now a game has to be in a game library folder, or fill the screen (borderless/fullscreen) and keep rendering, or be one you marked as a game.
- Launchers (Minecraft Launcher and other apps with "Launcher" in the name) are no longer treated as games. The game they start still is.
- Apps that 0.1.0/0.1.1 wrongly saved as games are cleared once. Real games are found again the next time you play.
- The tray menu has "*App* isn't a game" for anything Reticle gets wrong.
- More video and music apps are ignored (Stream Tube, FreeTube, Plex, Jellyfin, Kodi, Netflix, Spotify-style players and others).

larosa023/reticle.name: Reticle v0.1.1
larosa023/reticle.body:
## Reticle 0.1.1

**FPS now works reliably in the overlay.**

- **Fixed:** FPS stopped showing after you alt-tabbed out of a game for more than 20 seconds and came back. Frame capture now restarts every time a game comes to the front.
- **Fixed:** without admin rights the overlay only showed a dash for FPS. Reticle now sets this up with a single Windows prompt (never while a game is running): it starts with admin rights at sign-in from then on, and any later launch, from Hangar or elsewhere, switches to the admin copy without another prompt.
- Reticle now checks whether Windows actually allows frame capture, rather than just whether it's running as admin. A restricted admin token can't capture.
- Games that render from a helper process in their own folder are followed automatically.
- If an admin copy is already running, opening Reticle again goes to that copy instead of starting a second one.
- `reticle.log` now records, per game, whether frames arrived, which makes "no FPS" reports easy to diagnose.
- Every release is now tested on a real Windows machine: frame capture for D3D11 and D3D9, detecting a game and getting its FPS, alt-tabbing out and back in, and the switch to the admin copy.

larosa023/reticle.name: Reticle v0.1.0
larosa023/reticle.body:
## Reticle 0.1.0

The first release: a lightweight in-game performance overlay and crosshair, without injection.

- **Overlay**: FPS, frame time with a live graph, 1% and 0.1% lows, CPU usage and temperature, GPU usage, temperature, clock, power and VRAM (NVIDIA), RAM, clock and session length. Each one can be turned on or off.
- **Layouts**: full panel, compact line or FPS only. Pick a corner or drag it anywhere, and set the text size, opacity and colors. Each game remembers its own preset.
- **Automatic**: shows only while a game is in front and hides when you alt-tab.
- **Benchmarks**: record a run with a shortcut, then see average FPS, 1% and 0.1% lows and a frame-time graph. Runs are saved per game, and you can compare two of them or export a CSV.
- **Crosshair**: dot, cross, circle, T or your own PNG, with size, gap, thickness, color, outline and opacity settings. You turn it on or off per game.
- **Shortcuts**: Alt+Shift+O shows or hides the overlay, Alt+Shift+L cycles layouts, Alt+Shift+B starts or stops a benchmark, and Alt+Shift+X turns the crosshair on or off. You can change them all.
- **Safe with anti-cheat**: frame data comes from Windows' ETW graphics events, the way PresentMon gets it. Reticle never touches the game process.
- The 14 suite themes, accent colors and Hangar theme files. Tray icon, start with Windows, portable mode and a built-in updater with rollback.

Works over borderless and windowed games. Exclusive fullscreen hides any overlay window.

larosa023/pitstop.name: Pitstop 0.1.0
larosa023/pitstop.body:
## Pitstop 0.1.0

The first release: a clean NVIDIA driver manager that replaces the NVIDIA App.

- **Driver page:** your GPU, the installed driver and its branch, and the newest Game Ready and Studio drivers from NVIDIA with release notes.
- **Clean install:** official package from NVIDIA's servers only, signature-checked, unpacked down to the display driver (plus PhysX, HD Audio or USB-C if you want them). No NVIDIA App, no telemetry. Optional clean install and telemetry task removal.
- **Restore point** before every install (can be turned off).
- **Saved drivers:** the last 3 installed packages, reinstall any in one click.
- **Game settings:** search the driver's game profiles and change max frame rate, low latency mode, V-Sync, power management, texture filtering, shader cache size and G-SYNC. Export and import as a file.
- **History** of every install and rollback.
- **Tray alerts** for new drivers (optional), start with Windows.
- Admin rights only at the moment they're needed.
- Suite standards: 14 themes plus Hangar theme files, accent colors, built-in updater with Stable/Beta channels and automatic rollback, portable mode, `Ctrl+,` for Settings.

Download `Pitstop.exe` below. `SHA256SUMS.txt` has its checksum.

larosa023/halo.name: Halo v0.2.0
larosa023/halo.body:
## Halo 0.2.0: smoother, plus five new features

**Smooth at any refresh rate**
- Animation now runs at your monitor's own refresh rate (60, 144 or 240 Hz) and draws nothing while Halo sits idle.
- Hovers fade, the selected page and options slide, the battery number counts up, and pages glide in.
- Text layouts are cached, so each frame takes far less work.
- Turn on **Settings → Advanced → Frame rate counter** to see the rate.
- **Animations: Reduced** turns motion off. Halo also follows Windows' "Show animations" setting.

**New**
- **Automatic profiles per game:** attach apps to a profile ("Add a game or app" on each profile). While one of them is in front, Halo switches to that profile, and switches back to your settings when you leave it.
- **Hotkeys:** Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down steps through your DPI presets, and Ctrl+Alt+P goes to the next profile, from anywhere.
- **On-screen display:** a small popup at the bottom of the screen when DPI, polling rate or the profile changes from a hotkey, the tray or an automatic switch.
- **Battery history:** a 7-day graph on Overview, with how long the battery should last at your usual pace and when you last charged. The tray tooltip shows the time left too.
- **Polling test** (Performance): move the mouse and see the report rate Windows actually receives, with a peak and a live graph.
